data.cultural_impact: Tiffie was once a popular name for little girls in the English-speaking world. It was used as a diminutive form of more traditional and formal names such as Theodora, Matilda, or Dorothy. Today, however, the name Tiffie is less commonly used, and its cultural significance has largely faded away.

In the Bible, Jesus says, "Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these" (Matthew 19:14). This verse emphasizes the importance of welcoming and caring for children, and the name Tiffie may serve as a reminder of the preciousness and value of every child, no matter how small or insignificant they may seem in the eyes of the world. Furthermore, the name Tiffie may also convey a sense of playfulness and innocence, which are qualities associated with the childlike faith and trust in God that Jesus commends in the Bible.
